body_text:
A *path* (or parameterized curve) in an open set
$U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is a continuous mapping
$\gamma: [a, b] \to U$. The path is *piecewise continuously
differentiable* (or *piecewise smooth*) if the parameter
interval $[a, b]$ can be partitioned into finitely many
subintervals $a = t_0 < t_1 < \cdots < t_n = b$ such that
$\gamma$ has a continuous derivative $\gamma'(t)$ on each open
subinterval $(t_{k-1}, t_k)$ which extends to one-sided limits
at the endpoints.

The path is *closed* (a *loop*) if its initial and terminal
points coincide: $\gamma(a) = \gamma(b)$. It is *simple* if
$\gamma$ is injective on $[a, b)$ (no self-intersections). By
the Jordan Curve Theorem, every simple closed curve $\gamma$
divides the plane $\mathbb{C}$ into two connected components: a
bounded *interior* $\operatorname{Int}(\gamma)$ and an
unbounded *exterior* $\operatorname{Ext}(\gamma)$.
